title: Adaptations
seo_title: Primary 6 Science: Adaptations Worksheets (Structural and Behavioural, PSLE Practice)
standard_text: Recognise that adaptations are features or behaviours that help organisms survive in their habitats: to obtain food, escape from predators, breathe, move, and survive in extreme conditions. Distinguish structural and behavioural adaptations in plants and animals (summary of the MOE Primary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Primary 6 science worksheets for Singapore pupils on adaptations: structural and behavioural adaptations of mangrove trees, mudskippers, pitcher plants and more. PSLE practice with answers.
key_sub: Body parts are structural; actions are behavioural.
body_html:
How to think about it

An adaptation is a feature or behaviour that helps an organism survive in its habitat.

  • Structural adaptations are body parts: gills, webbed feet, breathing roots, a hard shell.
  • Behavioural adaptations are things the organism does: hunting at night, curling up, migrating.
  • Adaptations help organisms obtain food, escape predators, breathe, move, keep warm or cool, and reduce water loss.
  • Mangrove trees have breathing roots because the mud has little oxygen, and prop roots to hold them up in soft mud.
Example

A pangolin rolls into a ball when attacked. Structural or behavioural?

It is something the pangolin does

Answer: behavioural, to protect itself from predators

Example

A sunbird has a long, curved beak. How does this help it?

Think about what it eats

Answer: It reaches nectar deep inside flowers.

Common mistakes

  • Calling a behaviour (rolling into a ball, hunting at night) a structural adaptation.
  • Saying breathing roots take in water. They take in air.
  • Thinking an animal grows an adaptation because it wants or needs it during its life.
  • Forgetting that plants have adaptations too, such as floating leaves and spines.

faq.q: What is the difference between structural and behavioural adaptations?
faq.a: A structural adaptation is a body part, such as gills. A behavioural adaptation is something the organism does, such as hunting at night.

faq.q: How are mangrove trees adapted to their habitat?
faq.a: Breathing roots take in air from above the mud, and prop roots support the tree in the soft mud.
Yes. Water lilies have floating leaves, cacti have spines and pitcher plants trap insects.

items.q: How does the colour of a green grasshopper help it in a school field?
c: It helps it make food.
It blends in with the grass, so birds find it hard to see.
It helps it jump higher.
It keeps it cool.
items.e: Camouflage is a structural adaptation.

items.q: Which feature helps an olive-backed sunbird to reach the nectar deep inside flowers?

items.q: What is an adaptation?

items.q: What is a behavioural adaptation?

items.q: A spider spins a web. How does this help it survive?

It helps it take in oxygen dissolved in the water.
items.e: This adaptation helps the fish take in oxygen dissolved in the water.

items.q: A millipede curls up when it is touched. How does this help it survive?
c: It helps it warm up its body.
It helps it protect itself from predators.
It helps it escape the cold and find food.
It helps it hide from predators.
items.e: This adaptation helps the millipede protect itself from predators.

items.q: Which of these is a structural adaptation?
c: a small fish that swims in large groups called schools
a frog with a long, sticky tongue
a monitor lizard that lies in the sun in the morning
a dog that pants on a hot day
items.e: Structural adaptations are body parts. Behavioural adaptations are things an organism does.

items.q: A mudskipper has eyes on the top of its head. Which describes this adaptation?
c: a structural adaptation to spot predators while it lies in the water
a behavioural adaptation to spot predators while it lies in the water
a structural adaptation to catch prey that are active at night
a behavioural adaptation to catch prey that are active at night
items.e: A body part is a feature of its body, so it is a structural adaptation.

items.q: A Hydrilla plant has air spaces in its stems. How does this help it survive?
c: It helps it float near the surface where there is more light.
It helps it take in oxygen dissolved in the water.
It helps it catch insects for food.
It helps it reach the nectar deep inside flowers.
items.e: This adaptation helps the Hydrilla plant float near the surface where there is more light.

items.q: Ali saw a mudskipper rolling in the mud at low tide. What is the most likely reason?
c: to catch birds
to warm itself
to make food
to keep its skin wet so it can take in oxygen through its skin
items.e: Mudskippers can take in some oxygen through their wet skin.

items.q: A spider spins a web. Which describes this adaptation?
c: a behavioural adaptation to support itself in the soft mud
a behavioural adaptation to catch insects for food
a structural adaptation to catch insects for food
a structural adaptation to support itself in the soft mud
items.e: Something the animal does is a behaviour, so it is a behavioural adaptation.

items.q: Pitcher plants grow in poor, sandy soil in Singapore. Why do they trap insects?
c: to get nutrients that are lacking in the soil
to get sunlight
to get water
to protect their roots
items.e: They still make their own food by photosynthesis.

items.q: Which of these is a structural adaptation?
c: a monitor lizard that lies in the sun in the morning
an owl that hunts at night
a mangrove tree with breathing roots that stick up out of the mud
a spider that spins a web
items.e: Structural adaptations are body parts. Behavioural adaptations are things an organism does.

items.q: A desert animal comes out only at night. Which is the most likely reason?
c: to make food
to see better in sunlight
to avoid the heat of the day and lose less water
to find snow
items.e: Many desert animals are active at night.
